cards.explanation: The answer is his son. Jesus says the king "…prepared a wedding banquet for his son." (Matthew 22:2) The whole feast is in honor of the son, so this is no ordinary dinner. When somebody throws a party for their own child, you know the oven has been working overtime.

The answer is True. The king sends his servants to call those he had invited, "…but they refused to come." (Matthew 22:3) Read that slowly, friends. The invitation came from the king himself, and they said no. I have been shoved in a junk drawer, and even I would show up for THAT party.

The answer is that they ignore him and go off to work. They "…paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business." (Matthew 22:5) The king says everything is ready, and they walk off to their own stuff. I've kept a batch waiting while I finished one more little task, friends, but I never did it to a KING.

The answer is troops and city. "The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city." (Matthew 22:7) Troops fills the first blank, and city fills the second. This is a hard verse, friends. The text says the king was enraged, and it comes right after his servants were killed.

The answer is crossroads. The king says, "Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find." (Matthew 22:9) A crossroads is where roads meet and all kinds of people pass through. The servants are sent right where the foot traffic is.

The answer is False. The king says, "…invite to the banquet as many as you can find." (Matthew 22:9) He doesn't say to pick out the important ones. The goal is a full hall, and anyone the servants find counts.

The answer is both evil and good. The servants gathered "…everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests." (Matthew 22:10) Notice that it says everyone, friends. The hall fills up, and the invitation reaches far past the first guests.

The answer is that he isn't dressed in wedding clothes. "…when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes." (Matthew 22:11) Out of a whole hall, the king sees this one thing. The text doesn't tell us why the man didn't have them, and I won't guess.

The answer is speechless. The king asks, "how did you get in here without wedding clothes?" and "…the man was speechless." (Matthew 22:12) He has nothing to say, friends. I think that's a very quiet moment in that hall.

The answer is False. Jesus closes with "For many are called, but few are chosen." (Matthew 22:14) Many, then few, friends. Those two numbers are not twins. It's a short line, and I'd chew on it slowly, like a cookie fresh out of the oven.
